gap._description: Confirmed missing emissions (probe-verified: the analyzer emits nothing where the spec table requires an emission)

gaps.missing: import edges mislabeled reference_qualified (the tier classifier hardcodes reference_qualified for references, ignoring isImportDep — the JVM-family finding from java's pass) AND the edge source stays the 'root' placeholder (kotlin rewrites to the file's primary type; scala does not — family inconsistency)
gaps.evidence: probe: import java.util.List in class Importer -> 'root->java.util.List [references]/reference_qualified'

gaps.missing: pattern type references lost — case p: Point, case Point(a, b), case s: String emit NO reference to Point/String
gaps.evidence: probe: match { case p: Point => ... } emits only declared_type Int (case-class params) — no reference to Point

gaps.missing: Foo.bar method values emit no reference to Foo (the callable-reference analog of kotlin K3)
gaps.evidence: probe: xs.map(Foo.bar) emits only apply->map calls

gaps.missing: string interpolation s"hi $name" emits no Uses on name (kotlin K4 analog)
gaps.evidence: probe: s"hi $name x${n + 1}" emits no uses edge

gaps.missing: tuple-typed returns (Int, String) emit no type references (the return-type collector only matches generic_type/type_identifier/functional_type — tuple_type and compound/structural types are missed)
gaps.evidence: probe: def pair(): (Int, String) emits NO references to Int/String

gaps.missing: derives Show, Hashing emits no references to the derived types
gaps.evidence: probe: case class Person(name: String) derives Show emits no Person->Show reference

gaps.missing: type alias RHS references lost — type Fn = (Int) => String emits the Fn symbol (works) but NO references to Int/String from the alias's own definition
gaps.evidence: probe: type Fn = (Int) => String emits Fn[type] but no Fn->Int / Fn->String

gaps.missing: field accesses h.value (reads AND writes) emit no Uses on the receiver — scala has no field-access uses collector (only extension methods emit Uses); family gap vs java/groovy/kotlin
gaps.evidence: probe: h.value = h.value + 1 and read(h) = h.value emit zero uses

gaps.missing: self-type references lost — trait Logging { self: Service => } emits no reference to Service
gaps.evidence: probe: self: Service => emits no reference

decisions.question: a + b infix operator calls: Scala desugars to a.+(b) — a real method call. But operators are overwhelmingly stdlib/primitive (+, *, ::, map...) and there is no symbol table to filter user operators. Recommend: DECLARED LIMITATION (operator calls not emitted as Calls edges).
export scala.concurrent.duration.* — the export relationship kind is NOT EMITTED (pattern flag only). Recommend: DECLARED LIMITATION (consistent with kotlin S5 / groovy S3).

Parameterless method access without parens (xs.length, s.x) parses as field_expression — method vs field is indistinguishable without a symbol table. Recommend: fold into G8 — emit Uses on the RECEIVER only, never guess the selector kind.
XML literals: the grammar declares them but the analyzer ignores them entirely. Recommend: internal_silent (XML literal bodies are out of scope; embedding them would fabricate symbols).
(1, "a") tuple literal: an expression, not a declaration. Recommend: internal_silent (destructured locals are not symbols — consistent with kotlin S3).
Scala 3 macros: quote/splice expressions — handleCall already skips callees starting with a quote char (dotty-corpus fix). Recommend: internal_silent (macro AST manipulation is out of scope).
